title: Society Wives — Event-First Mature Fiction Writing Style
purpose: Mature adult ensemble romantic/sexual story writing: brief causal grounding, meaningful incident, natural immediate reaction, proportionate aftermath and flexible scene endings. Double meaning banter is optional, not the default engine.
rhythm: Flexible, non-mandatory: enter the scene where something worth reading can happen
One or two lines of existing familiarity or causal context, only if needed
Let the distinct incident or meaningful change carry the scene (planned or spontaneous)
Describe visible movement, immediate effect and actual character reaction without added interpretation
End naturally or transition; reflect later only if the next story event calls for it

narratorVisualDescription.origin: Reference technique from original Dhika EP03 (Chotu Babu intro): the narrator describes an apple-like silhouette in motion during a walk while another character notices it. This is narrator imagery, not a line spoken by the observing character.
narratorVisualDescription.appliesTo: All adult female characters in Society Wives, when scene-appropriate and approved by the author
methods: outfit fit, drape and fabric movement
standing stance, turn, weight shift and dance pose
narrator-only private observation distinct from spoken flirt
examplePhrases: apple-rounded silhouette with a gentle sway as she walked
athletic, sculpted outline and confident stride

useInstructions: Use specific, vivid, varied narrator descriptions rather than generic words such as beautiful, hot, curvy or sexy alone.
Link comparison to the action: walking vs standing vs turning vs dancing may reveal different visual details.
Show the relevant person's clothes, posture, movement and scene geometry; do not assume a figure description is a spoken compliment.
Distinguish narrator visual description, one person's caught glance, aloud joke and the woman's own awareness or reaction; do not merge those viewpoints.
Write distinct descriptions for Ankita, Sana, Aishwarya and other adult women; do not reuse the same apple metaphor mechanically across everyone.
If body shape/outfit has not been established, treat comparisons as optional proposal—not fixed character canon. Get author's direction before locking.
Keep all source-approved flirt, reaction and visual seeds; never quietly drop a user-specified beat. If something conflicts with canon, flag and ask before rewriting.
A glance, a smile, playful banter, accidental balancing contact and mutual interest are different narrative events; do not automatically infer any one from another.
Avoid gratuitous intrusion, underage sexualization, or sexualized family relationships. Any adult characters' boundaries and character reactions remain source-grounded.
sceneTemplate: What adult woman wears / visible fit?
Which comparison or visual detail would the narrator describe?
Which observer notices what, if anyone?
Does she catch a glance? What is her established response?
Do they speak, or is this only narrator POV?
How does it return to ordinary interaction?
narratorVisualDescription.writersNote: This extends the existing flirting/double-entendre rhythm; it never overrides the story master source, approved prose or user choice.

authorPacingRule.goal: Small encounters may have substantial effect. Match word count to dramatic event, not to number of people, pieces of contact, safety explanations or romance-stage milestones.
decisions: No obligatory buildup ladder: a character may already know another person, a surprise can occur, or backstory can be introduced in one or two lines when it matters.
Do not inflate ordinary hand/forearm/shoulder actions into key erotic or romantic milestones just to make familiarity seem earned.
Do not require one physical touch, one witty comeback, one fluster and one emotional debrief per character in an ensemble.
Let a concrete incident, a sudden change in proximity, a meaningful choice, a look or an immediate character reaction earn scene attention; vary mechanisms naturally.
If an event is accidental, intentional, misunderstood or spontaneous, give only enough local causality to make it believable. Do not pre-seed every future beat.
Use double meaning banter selectively: dialogue is strongest when it naturally reflects this particular person's voice and creates an event, not when it substitutes for one.
Narrator describes bodies/clothing/movement in context when useful; distinguish observer's perspective and what the focal character actually knows.
Do not invent additional regret, fear, desire, trust or consent just because one reaction occurred; do not ban longer introspection when an actual later incident requires it.
Preserve source-approved events and timeline; no silent rewriting, no public approval claims for a draft, no copying Dhika incidents word for word.
Perform continuity checks privately. The prose itself should not read like an editor's checklist, repeated safety disclaimer or psychological interpretation.
Allow ordinary goodbyes and hard cuts. Meaningful events need not each conclude a complete relationship arc.
authorPacingRule.authorDirection: Author correction 16 Nov 2026: Stop overprotective and overly controlled banter/hand-touch narration. Preserve genre, vivid physical immediacy, unexpected but plausible moments and room for later discoveries.

sourceGroundedNarrativeCalibration.title: Dhika source study — compact setup, high-impact incident, optional later interpretation
sourceGroundedNarrativeCalibration.sourceScope: Dhika EP01–EP03 directly reviewed; selected EP04–EP06 continuation passages checked; NOT an exhaustive read of 41 archived episodes

diagnosis.correction: No compulsory hand-touch → comfort → emotional analysis progression. Events can arrive after one-line backstory or without foreshadowing.
Keep each voice distinct, use only necessary exchanges, then let event and immediate reaction hold the scene.
Natural clear physical staging, not body-contact route maps and one token touch per person.
Write only reaction actually warranted now. Brief goodbyes are valid; later retrospective depth is also valid when needed.
A crowded ensemble needs a coherent lived-in environment, not a five-pair escalation matrix.
Backfill history later, introduce surprise, and preserve possibilities not yet ruled out by approved source.
Do not use repeated editorial justifications to interrupt narration; preserve factual knowledge and agency in actual action/reaction.

sourceObservations: EP01 introduces character/world only; Bantu–Bobby's first on-page exchange is EP02.
EP02 gives Bantu–Bobby recurring familiarity in a few lines alongside immediate compliments and distinct personalities.

EP03 is a short college conversation followed by a specific journey incident, ordinary drop-off and then a separate Chotu household plot; Chotu's prior year of familiarity is summarized, not staged as many prior episodes.
EP04 uses longer retrospective feelings when a later event calls for them; never claim that Dhika never reflects.
EP05 backfills marriage history partway through the story; later history can be given at the moment it becomes dramatically useful.
Do not draw unsupported claims about later unseen episodes; inspect before assertion.
principles: Event first; prior context in one or two lines if sufficient.
Unexpected action can be plausible without a predefined sequence of incremental gestures.
Immediate precise reaction beats lengthy generalized psychology.
Non-graphic adult physical tension is not interchangeable with a hand/shoulder touch checklist.
Banter supports, but never replaces, a memorable action.
Visual narrator observations use the chosen body's movement/wardrobe and are not a spoken dialogue by default.
Use the other characters' knowledge and secrets without forcing the heroine to know what the reader knows.
Normal cut, practical transition or later reflective chapter are all valid endings depending on what actually happens.
Preserve room for future characters, encounters and surprises; avoid dating or defining unapproved arcs.
No forced uniform episode pacing or mandatory emotional debrief.
prohibitions: No compulsory psychological ladder or relationship-definition after every contact.
No mandatory safe hand/forearm/shoulder staging as a substitute for substantive event.
No repeated five-to-ten-turn banter merely to stretch a scene.
No unilateral rewriting of approved character thoughts, physical reactions, dates or published prose.
No blanket claim about future Dhika episodes based only on the early three.
No generic genre-softening of requested adult romantic/sexual tension into an innocuous workplace drama.
No fake future canon, reciprocal interest or unseen physical actions inferred from one glance.
sourceGroundedNarrativeCalibration.plotSuggestionFormat: If an outline is requested, return compact title/time/cast, one-line context, the distinctive new incident, immediate source-faithful reaction, and exit. These headings are optional editorial metadata, NOT required scene prose.
sourceGroundedNarrativeCalibration.proseStandard: Continuous natural Hinglish; short lived-in context; character-specific voice and body/wardrobe/motion observation when relevant; clear event, immediate effect and no compulsory explanation afterward.
sourceGroundedNarrativeCalibration.previousApprovedStories: Do not rewrite Ankita, Meenakshi, Shivani, Taniya, Soniya or Shreya approved material merely to apply a new style guide.

authorRevisionNotes20261117.focus: Short event-first accidents, private staging, exact author-provided numbers, selective graphical-insertion markers and minimal aftermath
mistakesIdentified: Public audience staging invented for a private two-observer accident; a crowd would change the stakes into unwanted public shame
Explicit author-specified figure one-third (1/3) was omitted from the visual continuity requirements
A simple official journey and a 5–6-second mishap expanded into unnecessary filler dialogue and psychological explanation
A brief normal exit became a separate overlong aftermath; repeated explanations buried the incident
Placeholder markers treated as a fixed quota instead of matching scene-specific and author-specific visual needs
Original Dhika EP01–EP03 compression and bodily reaction examples were not followed as a pacing reference
mandatoryRules: Preserve every author-specified numeric quantity, exact fraction, time, physical extent, count, and spatial constraint in planning and relevant drafting; DO NOT replace 1/3 by 'small part' or an invented value. Render numerals naturally where they matter.

A private exposure or observation intended only for two named characters must be spatially private: no public sightline, crowd, third witness, staged embarrassment or involuntary shared audience. Physical cause and viewpoint must be credible.
Describe an accidental incident in a compact event-focused passage, not multi-paragraph psychology. A five-to-six-second observation is ONE continuous instant, not two inflated separate sequences.

Use one or more GROK/author visual markers solely when an identified visual, physical movement, or observation genuinely needs further user-directed insertion. There is NO fixed minimum or maximum marker count; zero, one, two or many are possible.

Do not silently convert author-marked visual material into generic non-visual prose or dilute the numbered visibility boundary. Keep the marker and the author's continuity constraints intact when the insertion itself is not yet authored.

If requested marker density would dominate the story or shift tone toward a porn-like montage, explain the tonal consequence and offer a more focused marker layout; let the author decide scene emphasis. Do not automatically insert extra visual beats.

Pace setup by causal necessity: Beat 07 a brief arrival, Beat 08 one private accident with immediate genuine reaction, Beat 09 a two-to-three-line exit plus logistical bridge to the next training beat.
Differentiate Karan's briefly broken teasing from Aman's restrained practical response; no invented lasting guilt, mutual desire, memory monologue or next-episode promise.
Follow the Dhika EP01–EP03 comparative style reference for concise build/action/response; preserve longer passages only when event stakes actually warrant them.
Existing approved prose stays immutable without explicit author instruction. A revision draft for Beats 07–09 is NOT automatic approval or publication.
